source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 902 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-902.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 902 was established by Ordinance No. 29262, passed by the Dallas City Council on January 22, 2014. (Ord. 29262)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-902.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 902 is established on property located on the south corner of Corning Avenue and Lancaster Road. The size of PD 902 is approximately 3.3596 acres. (Ord. 29262)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-902.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district may be developed in phases.

(d) This district is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. 29262)

sections.title: Exhibits
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-902.104. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this article:

(1) Exhibit 902A: Tract I, Phase 2 and Tract II conceptual plan.

(2) Exhibit 902B: Tract I, Phase 1 development plan.

(3) Exhibit 902C: Tract I, Phase 1 landscape plan. (Ord. 29262)

sections.title: Conceptual Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-902.105. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of Tract I, Phase 2 and Tract II must comply with the Tract I, Phase 2 and Tract II conceptual plan (Exhibit 902A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the Tract I, Phase 2 and Tract II conceptual plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 29262)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-902.106. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) Tract I.

(1) Phase 1. Development and use of the Property must comply with the Tract I, Phase 1 development plan (Exhibit 902B). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the Tract I, Phase 1 development plan, the text of this article controls.

(2) Phase 2. A development plan must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of any building permit to authorize work in this phase. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls.

(b) Tract II.

(1) In general. Except as provided in this subsection, no development plan is required, and the provisions of Section 51A-4.702 regarding submission of or amendments to a development plan, site analysis plan, conceptual plan, and development schedule do not apply.

(2) Multifamily. For multifamily uses, a development plan must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of any building permit to authorize work in this tract. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 29262)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-902.107. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Tract I. The only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the CR Community Retail District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the CR Community Retail District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the CR Community Retail District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the CR Community Retail District is subject to DIR in this district; etc.

(b) Tract II. The only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the MF-1(A) Multifamily District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the MF-1(A) Multifamily District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the MF-1(A) Multifamily District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review
(DIR) in the MF-1(A) Multifamily District is subject to DIR in this district; etc. (Ord. 29262)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-902.108. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A- 4.217.

(b) The following accessory use is permitted by right:

-- Accessory community center (private). (Ord. 29262)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-902.109. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) Tract I.

(1) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the CR Community Retail District apply.

(2) Side yard. Minimum side yard is 15 feet.

(3) Height. Maximum structure height is 35 feet.

(4) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 30 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(5) Stories. Maximum number of stories above grade is two.

(b) Tract II.

(1) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the MF-1(A) Multifamily District apply.

(2) Side and rear yard. Minimum side yard is 15 feet. No minimum rear yard.

(3) Density. Maximum number of dwelling units is 50.

(4) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 60 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(5) Lot size. No minimum lot size.

(6) Stories. Maximum number of stories above grade is three. (Ord. 29262)

sections.title: Fence
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-902.110. FENCE.

(a) Tract I. A minimum six-foot solid fence is required along the property line adjacent to residential uses.

(b) Tract II. A minimum six-foot perimeter fence is required. The perimeter fence may be constructed of wrought iron, masonry, wood, or any combination thereof. (Ord. 29262)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-902.111. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general.

(1) Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A- 4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(2) Parking is permitted in the required front and side yard setbacks.

(b) Tract I. For purposes of off-street parking, the entire Property is considered one lot.

(c) Tract II.

(1) Accessory community center (private). No off-street parking is required.

(2) Screening. Screening is required for all surface parking lots. (Ord. 29262)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-902.112. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 29262)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-902.113. LANDSCAPING.

(a) In general.

(1) Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(2) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition.

(b) Tract I.

(1) Applicability of Article X. Increasing the amount of non-permeable coverage on a lot does not trigger compliance with Article X.

(2) Phase 1. For a restaurant with drive-in or drive-through service, landscaping must be provided as shown on the Tract I, Phase 1 landscape plan (Exhibit 902C). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the Tract I, Phase 1 landscape plan, the text of this article controls.

(3) Phase 2.

(A) A landscape plan must be submitted with the development plan and approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of a building permit to authorize work in this phase.

(B) Trees with a minimum caliper of two inches may be substituted for street trees.

(4) Perimeter landscape buffer strip.

(A) A building site is exempt from the residential adjacency requirements.

(B) A minimum five-foot landscape buffer is required.

(c) Tract II.

(1) Landscape plan. A landscape plan must be submitted with the development plan and approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of a building permit to authorize work in this tract.

(2) Perimeter landscape buffer strip. A building site is exempt from the residential adjacency requirements.

(3) Design standards. The design standards in Section 51A-10.126 do not apply. (Ord. 29262)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-902.114. SIGNS.

(a) Except as provided in this section, signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) The requirement in Section 51A-7.301 that attached signs within 100 feet of private property in a non-business zoning district or a public park of more than one acre must comply with Division 51A-7.400 does not apply to flat attached signs illuminated with neon in Tract I, Phase 1.

(c) The prohibition in Section 51A-7.303 on changes of illumination producing an apparent motion of a visual image does not apply to flat attached signs illuminated with neon in Tract I, Phase 1. (Ord. 29262)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-902.115. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) The screening of dumpsters is permitted to cross lot lines. Dumpsters are permitted in the rear yard setbacks.

(c) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 29262)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-902.116. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 29262)
